prompt_en: An intimate documentary photograph of a woman with reference-guided face and hair in a soil-centered work scene. A restoration is in progress inside a small daylight atelier. She is seated at a scarred wooden bench, repairing an old ochre earthen-plaster relief panel that rests almost flat on a padded wooden support. One dry corner has flaked away, and the fallen matching chip lies beside it among angular clods and fine sandy earth. Her left palm steadies the sound outer edge of the panel; her right hand holds a short palette knife, its flat blade actually contacting the broken recess and pressing darker damp earth paste into it. Both forearms are visible and lead naturally back to her shoulders. A short part of the fissure is already bridged by a moist, slightly raised repair, while the remaining pale brittle fracture stays visible next to it. The place where the blade ends, the freshly filled section, and the unrepaired edge are all easy to distinguish. A shallow bowl of damp earthy paste sits within reach on the right side of the bench. In the foreground, a small mortar contains crushed ochre soil, and a wire sieve rests above a tray of powder, connecting raw earth to the repair. Soil is materially legible as granular powder, rough dry clods, and a cohesive wet patch, with tiny mineral grains visible in the old panel. The fresh filler makes a bounded reddish-brown soil patch in the broken corner; tiny embedded grains share the patch's reddish-brown hue, which ends at the ragged contact with the older pale ochre panel. A dusty rust-colored handprint marks the front of her oatmeal canvas apron, and a smear of the same wet earth clings to her right thumb beside the knife grip. Her visible oval face, large brown eyes, small straight nose, softly flushed cheeks and pink lips retain the supplied reference's proportions; her glossy dark chin-length bob and fine airy center-parted fringe retain its silhouette. She looks down toward the seam with a softened brow and gently parted lips, caught between concentration and relief as the material begins to hold. A simple cream sleeveless cotton top under the apron and loose hair framing her cheek give a quiet, intimate human warmth. A landscape three-quarter medium view from across the bench keeps her face, connected arms, apron transfer and repair on the same visual plane. Soft side window light rakes across the earthen surfaces; restrained ochre and cream tones, realistic pores and cotton fibers, moderate depth of field, an unhurried lived-in atelier impression.
